How does a chat room receive new messages in real time?

A connection that stays open, letting both sides send messages at any time·Live chat and collaborative editing may use WebSocket when both sides need frequent messages. An HTTP request and response form one message exchange, but the underlying HTTP connection can be reused and HTTP/2 can multiplex streams. After its handshake, WebSocket exchanges messages in both directions over one connection. Messages arriving within the polling interval are delayed; shorter intervals cost more requests.

Where message delay comes from in each

Polling waits for the next check: A new message may wait for the next check; shorter intervals mean more requests.

WebSocket can send proactively: An open connection lets the server send proactively, but actual delay also depends on server work, queues, network, and client rendering.

Both sides can send: It is not just server push: the client can send anytime over the same connection.

What people often confuse

A WebSocket does not guarantee the connection never drops: network switches and server restarts disconnect it, so auto-reconnect is needed. It fits real-time scenarios with frequent two-way traffic; ordinary page reads work fine with ordinary requests.

Auto-reconnect on disconnection; afterward confirm it is a persistent connection in the Network panel and test that messages resume after a network recovery.
